idea-plugin.name: Kei - API Contract Testing
idea-plugin.description:
API contract checks for JavaScript and TypeScript calls

Kei finds the OpenAPI 3.x and Swagger 2.0 contracts in your project and checks fetch and axios calls in JavaScript/TypeScript against them while you edit.

Contract discovery

  • Indexes YAML/JSON files whose name contains openapi, swagger or api and that declare an OpenAPI/Swagger version (node_modules, build, dist, target and similar folders are skipped)
  • Re-indexes contract files when they change; Tools → Refresh Contracts re-scans on demand
  • Kei Contracts tool window: endpoints, request body fields (required fields marked with *) and responses

Call validation (JavaScript/TypeScript, needs the bundled JavaScript plugin)

  • fetch(url, { method, body }) and axios.get/post/put/patch/delete(url, body) with a string-literal URL
  • Path templates such as /users/{id} match concrete URLs such as /users/42; host, query string and a base-path prefix are ignored
  • Object-literal request bodies (also inside JSON.stringify): missing required fields, literal type mismatches and invalid enum values
  • Optional weak warning for calls with no matching contract endpoint
  • Quick fix (Alt+Enter): add a missing required field with a placeholder value

Settings: Settings → Tools → Kei API Contract Testing. Free and open source (Apache-2.0).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.9.0

  • Calls to concrete URLs (/users/42, absolute URLs, URLs with query strings) now match templated contract paths (/users/{id}); previously only the literal template text matched.
  • Swagger 2.0 contracts are now parsed (only OpenAPI 3 worked) and local $ref request schemas are resolved.
  • "Add missing field" quick fix no longer produces invalid code (missing comma) when the object already has properties.
  • Settings were not saved and had no effect; they are now persisted per project and respected by the inspection and the file watcher.
  • Deleting or editing a contract file no longer leaves stale endpoints in the index; file events from other projects are ignored.
  • The "no contract found" warning is no longer reported in projects without any contract.
  • axios method detection no longer misreads calls such as axios.getUri.
  • The inspection was registered twice (also without the JavaScript plugin installed).
  • Indexing no longer runs on an unmanaged coroutine scope or parses files on the UI thread.
  • Refresh Contracts action is now available in the Tools menu.
  • Changed: Built with the IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.x; the plugin no longer bundles its own copy of kotlinx-coroutines.
  • Changed: Plugin description and README describe only the features that exist (GraphQL, mock server, diff viewer, analytics and other advertised features were never implemented).
  • Removed: Unreachable code (security analyzer, documentation/CI/client/performance generators, history/diff/analytics helpers, mock data generator), the GraphQL stub, the unused graphql-java and json-schema-validator dependencies, and stale build/marketing documents.

2026.8.0

  • The plugin is now completely free — all features unlocked, no license needed.
  • Source code is now open source under Apache-2.0: https://github.com/JirakJ/api-contract-guard

2026.3.15

  • Quick fixes now create PSI via the public PsiFileFactory API instead of internal JavaScript plugin classes

2025.11.1

  • Initial release: OpenAPI contract discovery, contract explorer and fetch/axios validation with quick fixes
